title: Unique sums give domain monoid algebras
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative integral domain and $M$ a commutative additive monoid with the following unique-sums property: for every nonempty finite $A,B\subseteq M$ there are $a_0\in A,b_0\in B$ for which $a+b=a_0+b_0$, $a\in A,b\in B$, implies $(a,b)=(a_0,b_0)$. Form $R[M]=\bigoplus_{m\in M}Re^m$, with $e^me^n=e^{m+n}$. For $f,h\in R[M]$, if $a_0\in\operatorname{supp}(f)$ and $b_0\in\operatorname{supp}(h)$ and $(a_0,b_0)$ uniquely represents its sum among pairs in their supports, then $(fh)_{a_0+b_0}=f_{a_0}h_{b_0}$. The ring $R[M]$ is an integral domain. Additive monoid conventions are those of [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup].
